title: idol: one photo becomes a 3D model

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: You need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA for your own runs; two encoder models ask you to accept their terms once; and it is built for single objects, not scenes.

verify_before_render: Every point cites its source in the plan (model-idol-01/plan.json).
Kit images are drawn from the plan's own visual spec only.

scenes.heading: ONE PHOTO, NOW 3D
scenes.say: What if your product photo could spin around — in full 3D?

scenes.heading: ONE PICTURE, FULL 3D
scenes.say: idol turns one single picture into a full three-D Gaussian splat, even the sides your camera never saw.

scenes.heading: BACKGROUND CUT, PLY OUT
scenes.say: It removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard PLY file, so it opens in any splat viewer or Blender.

scenes.heading: RUNS ON YOUR GPU
scenes.say: And it runs on your own graphics card: seven point two gigabytes of VRAM, and under two seconds on a fast card.

scenes.heading: TRY IT FREE
scenes.say: Try it free in the browser demo, or install the SDK and call it from one line of Python.

scenes.heading: TOP OF THE TABLE TODAY
scenes.say: On their own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual score, and it is the top trending model today.

scenes.heading: WHAT TO EXPECT
scenes.say: You need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA for your own runs; two encoder models ask you to accept their terms once; and it is built for single objects, not scenes.

idea: idol turns one picture of an object into a full three-D Gaussian splat — background cut, .ply out — on a consumer GPU and free to try.

claims.text: idol turns a single picture of an object into a full three-D Gaussian splat, including the sides the picture never showed.
The pipeline removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard 3DGS .ply that opens in any Gaussian splat viewer.
It runs on consumer GPUs: 7.2 GB of VRAM, and can run in under 2 seconds.
You can try it free in the Hugging Face Space, or install the open SDK and call it from Python.
On the lab's own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual column, and it was the number-one trending model on Hugging Face today.
